heading: Changes in v2.0.0
body:
v2.0.0 adds [cancellation](#cancellation). No API was removed, but two changes can break an application that worked with v1.x:

- **A new message type.** A cancel goes to the peer as a message of type `4`, `constants.type.CANCEL`. A v1.x peer does not know it and fails the session with an `RPCError` with the code `UNKNOWN_MESSAGE`. Update both ends before either of them cancels. The ports to other languages added it in `bare-rpc-swift` v3.0.0, `bare-rpc-kotlin` v0.6.0, and `bare-rpc-python` v0.3.0. A v1.x caller still works with a v2.0.0 peer, as it never sends a cancel.
- **Destroying a reply stream cancels the request.** Destroying the stream from `createResponseStream()` before the end of the reply has arrived cancels the request, which also destroys its request stream and tells the peer to stop. Breaking out of a `for await` loop over the stream destroys it. In v1.x, it destroyed only the reply stream. Against a v1.x peer, this fails the session as described above, even if the application never calls `cancel()`.
